title: 77. Numeracy & Number Systems: Converting Nonnegative Integers Between Binary and Decimal
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a binary integer to its decimal value.
questions.question: What is the decimal value of \(1000_2\)?
questions.explanation: From left to right, the place values are \(2^3\), \(2^2\), \(2^1\), \(2^0\). Only \(2^3\) contributes, so \(1000_2=8\). The value \(16\) shifts every exponent one position too far.
questions.hint: Assign binary place values from left to right, ending with the units place.

questions.concept: Decimal-to-Binary Conversion of a Four-Digit Representation
questions.learningObjective: Convert a nonnegative decimal integer to binary using powers of two.
questions.question: Which binary number represents the decimal number \(9\)?
questions.explanation:
Write \(9\) as a sum of powers of \(2\):
\[
9 = 8+1 = 2^3+2^0
\]
In binary place values, this gives \(1\times 2^3+0\times 2^2+0\times 2^1+1\times 2^0\), which is \(1001_2\). Therefore, \(9=1001_2\). The alternative sets an additional bit.
questions.hint: Express the decimal number as a sum of powers of \(2\).

questions.concept: Binary-to-Decimal Conversion of a Five-Digit Representation
questions.learningObjective: Convert a binary integer to decimal using place values.
questions.question: What is the decimal value of \(11010_2\)?
questions.explanation:
Use binary place values:
\[
11010_2 = 1\times 2^4 + 1\times 2^3 + 0\times 2^2 + 1\times 2^1 + 0\times 2^0
\]
This equals \(16+8+0+2+0=26\). Therefore, \(11010_2=26\). The alternative omits the contribution of the \(2^1\) place.
questions.hint: Write the number in expanded form using powers of \(2\).

questions.concept: Decimal-to-Binary Conversion of a Five-Digit Representation
questions.learningObjective: Convert a nonnegative decimal integer to binary using powers of two.
questions.question: Which binary number represents the decimal number \(23\)?
questions.explanation:
Write \(23\) as a sum of powers of \(2\):
\[
23 = 16+4+2+1 = 2^4+2^2+2^1+2^0
\]
Therefore, the binary representation is \(10111_2\). The choice "\(11011_2\)" equals \(27\).
questions.hint: Find the largest power of \(2\) not exceeding \(23\), then continue with the remainder.

questions.concept: Binary-to-Decimal Conversion of a Six-Digit Representation
questions.learningObjective: Convert a binary integer to decimal using place values.
questions.question: What is the decimal value of \(111001_2\)?
questions.explanation:
Use binary place values:
\[
111001_2 = 32+16+8+0+0+1 = 57
\]
Therefore, \(111001_2=57\). The alternative adds a contribution from a zero bit.
questions.hint: Add the powers of \(2\) represented by each \(1\) in the binary number.

questions.concept: Decimal-to-Binary Conversion of a Six-Digit Representation
questions.learningObjective: Convert a nonnegative decimal integer to binary using powers of two.
questions.question: Which binary number represents the decimal number \(50\)?
questions.explanation:
Write \(50\) as a sum of powers of \(2\):
\[
50 = 32+16+2 = 2^5+2^4+2^1
\]
Therefore, the binary representation is \(110010_2\). The choice "\(101010_2\)" equals \(42\).
questions.hint: Use the largest powers of \(2\) that sum to \(50\).

questions.concept: Binary-to-Decimal Conversion of a Six-Digit Representation
questions.learningObjective: Convert a binary integer to decimal using place values.
questions.question: What is the decimal value of \(100101_2\)?
questions.explanation:
Use binary place values:
\[
100101_2 = 32+0+0+4+0+1 = 37
\]
Therefore, \(100101_2=37\). The alternative replaces a set bit with one of smaller place value.
questions.hint: Match each \(1\) to its place value and add them.

questions.concept: Converting an Integer with Separated Set Bits
questions.learningObjective: Convert a nonnegative decimal integer to binary.
questions.question: Which binary number represents the decimal integer \(44\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(44=32+8+4=2^5+2^3+2^2\). These positions give \(101100_2\). The alternative omits the \(2^3\) contribution and represents \(36\).
questions.hint: Express the integer as a sum of distinct powers of two.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize the binary representation of zero.
questions.question: Which binary numeral represents the decimal integer \(0\)?
questions.explanation: No place value contributes to zero, so its binary numeral is \(0_2\). The numeral \(1_2\) represents one.
questions.hint: Consider which binary digit has zero contribution.

questions.concept: Binary-to-Decimal Conversion of a Six-Digit Representation
questions.learningObjective: Convert a binary integer to decimal using place values.
questions.question: What is the decimal value of \(101101_2\)?
questions.explanation:
Use binary place values:
\[
101101_2 = 32+0+8+4+0+1 = 45
\]
Therefore, \(101101_2=45\). The alternative omits or shifts a set-bit contribution.
questions.hint: Write the number as a sum of powers of \(2\), including only the positions where a \(1\) appears.
